case_name: Sri Srinivasa Theatre and Others v Government Of Tamil Nadu And Ors.
facts: The case involves a batch of writ petitions filed by various cinema theatres against the Tamil Nadu Government.
The theatres are challenging the validity of certain provisions in the Tamil Nadu Entertainment Tax Act, 1939.
The main issue is whether the classification of theatres based on their location and the method of taxation imposed on them is reasonable and constitutional.
issues: Whether the classification of theatres based on their location is reasonable and constitutional
Whether the method of taxation imposed on the theatres is confiscatory and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution
petitioner_arguments: The Act classifies theatres situated in a local area into two categories, subjecting one category to a hostile treatment.
The classification is arbitrary, unreasonable, and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution.
The impugned provision seeks to treat unequals equally, which itself is a negation of the guarantee of equal protection of laws.
respondent_arguments: The classification of theatres based on their location is reasonable and constitutional.
The method of taxation imposed on the theatres is not confiscatory and does not violate Article 14 of the Constitution.
court_reasoning: The court held that the classification of theatres based on their location is unreasonable and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution.
The court also held that the method of taxation imposed on the theatres is confiscatory and violative of Article 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.
holding: The court allowed the writ petitions and declared the impugned provisions of the Tamil Nadu Entertainment Tax Act, 1939 to be unconstitutional.
The court held that the classification of theatres based on their location is unreasonable and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution.
